questions.q: What is the magnetic effect of electric current?
questions.a: A current-carrying wire sets up a magnetic field around it, shown by a deflecting compass.

questions.q: How can you make a current's magnetic effect stronger?
questions.a: Increase the current or coil the wire many turns (make an electromagnet).

questions.q: Who first showed that current produces magnetism?
questions.a: Hans Christian Oersted, by deflecting a compass needle with a current.
A soft iron core with a coil around it; current in the coil makes it a strong magnet that can be switched off.
Cranes lifting iron scrap, and electric bells, fans and motors.

questions.q: How can an electromagnet be made weaker or stronger?
questions.a: Less or more current, fewer or more turns, or removing the iron core.

questions.q: What is the heating effect of current?
questions.a: Current heats the wire it passes through - the basis of heaters, toasters and fuses.

questions.q: Why is nichrome used in heater coils?
questions.a: Nichrome has high resistance, so it heats strongly without melting.

questions.q: How does a fuse use the heating effect?
questions.a: Too much current melts the fuse wire, breaking the circuit and stopping damage.

questions.q: How does a battery generate electricity?
questions.a: Chemical reactions inside the cell separate charges, making a potential difference that drives current in a circuit.

questions.q: Name the two terminals of a cell.
questions.a: Positive (metal cap) and negative (metal disc) terminals.

questions.q: What happens to the chemicals of a dry cell as it works?
questions.a: They get used up, so the cell 'runs down' and stops driving current.
